note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: watery diarrhea for ~3 days, described as very loose/watery stools "pouring straight" from the rectum.
- Frequency/timing: occurring almost hourly while awake.
- Onset/progression: started ~3 days ago and not improving.
- Associated symptoms: crampy lower/mid abdominal pain (intermittent, ~6/10 when present), nausea, at least one episode of vomiting after drinking milk, subjective feeling of being hot (no temperature measured), decreased urine frequency.
- Stool characteristics: very watery, no recall of blood.
- Exposures/contacts: brother has had a similar illness for ~5 days.
- Diet/trigger: milk provoked vomiting; had lunch today but stool remained loose.
- Functional impact: difficulty going to work; attempting to maintain oral fluids.

Past Medical History:
- Reports otherwise fit and well; no chronic medical conditions disclosed.
- Medications: Paracetamol recently used (dose/route/frequency not documented). No regular medications.
- Allergies: none known ("I don't have any allergies that I know of").
- Family history: father with colon cancer (patient reports "stage three", details uncertain).
- Social: lives with mother and sister; brother lives separately. Occupation: office-based government work in Central London. Social smoker (occasional) and drinks alcohol occasionally (binge social drinking once or twice a month).

Physical Examination:
- Telephonic/teleconsult note: video/visual connection poor; assessment primarily history-based.
- Reported/observed findings:
  - Patient reports feeling very hot; no measured temperature recorded.
  - Vomited once after milk ingestion.
  - Passing urine but less frequently than usual.
  - No blood reported in stool.
  - Intermittent crampy abdominal pain (lower/mid abdomen).
  - Patient communicative via audio.

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis (watery diarrhoea with crampy abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting) — clinician expressed concern for fluid/mineral losses and potential dehydration.

Management Plan:
- Conservative/outpatient management advised:
  - Advise increased oral fluids; recommend oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte) available over the counter (no prescription required).
  - Clear fluids initially; progress to a soft diet (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated.
  - Paracetamol for fever/pain is appropriate (paracetamol already being used; dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Advise avoidance of alcohol while unwell.
- Safety-netting/follow-up:
  - If symptoms are not settling within 48 hours (i.e., 1–2 days), patient instructed to call back for further assessment.
  - If signs of dehydration develop, further investigations and management will be required (specific investigations not specified in the consult).
- No medicines were prescribed during the consult.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 3 days of frequent watery diarrhoea (hourly while awake), intermittent crampy abdominal pain, nausea and one episode of vomiting after milk; brother had similar illness. Likely gastroenteritis with concern for ongoing fluid/electrolyte losses. Management: oral rehydration (Diarolyte), clear fluids/soft diet, paracetamol PRN; return if not improved in 48 hours or if dehydration worsens.

Key Takeaways:
- Maintain hydration; use an oral rehydration solution (Diarolyte) available OTC.
- Use paracetamol for fever or pain as needed.
- Avoid alcohol and gradually reintroduce a soft diet as tolerated.

Next Steps:
- Patient to obtain Diarolyte (OTC) and prioritize rehydration.
- Monitor symptoms and urine output; if not improving within 48 hours or if dehydration signs worsen, contact clinic for further evaluation and investigations (not specified).
- No immediate tests ordered during this consult.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate) not recorded.
  - Physical abdominal examination and other exam findings not available (teleconsult, video poor).
  - Exact stool frequency count/day and stool volume not precisely quantified.
  - Detailed medication reconciliation and exact paracetamol dosing not documented.
  - No specific criteria documented for dehydration assessment.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Doctor states "OK so you're feeling hoarse" though the patient did not report hoarseness elsewhere in the conversation — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio-only consult with poor/absent video; some overlapping speech and minor disfluency but overall history is intelligible.
